subject: Renewal kickoff: DataSentry commitment, capacity uplift & QBR scheduling
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Alex Barnes <alex@datasentry.com>; Samantha Lee <samantha@datasentry.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal kickoff: DataSentry commitment, capacity uplift & QBR scheduling

Hi Alex / Samantha —

Thanks for taking the call earlier. Per our conversation, I wanted to start the renewal kickoff thread so we have a single place for timeline, owners, and next steps. High level summary below and asks at the end.

Summary
- Current term expires: 2026-09-30.
- Proposed renewal: 12-month term (Oct 1, 2026 — Sep 30, 2027) with a capacity uplift to accommodate expected production growth.
- Proposed uplift: +200k tokens/day burst capacity (we recommend tier bump from Standard -> Pro for predictable unit economics).
- Primary checkpoints: legal review / SOW sign, procurement terms, QBR within 2 weeks of renewal effective date, onboarding runbook for capacity ramp.

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (SOW + service description), capacity_pricing_2026-08.xlsx (pricing scenarios).

Preliminary timeline (proposed)
1) 2026-08-16 — Kickoff + confirm attendee list and billing contact (today).
2) 2026-08-18 — Redwood sends final SOW for legal redline (we can fast-track if procurement needs).
3) 2026-08-21 — DocuSign envelope goes to procurement (aim).
4) 2026-09-01 — Preferred QBR window (see poll below) to review runbook and ramp plan prior to effective date.

Owners
- Redwood AM / Renewal lead: Olga Petrov (me) — overall cadence, calendar, runbook.
- Redwood Pricing/Commercial: Rishi Malhotra — final pricing and tier confirmation.
- Customer Exec Sponsor: Alex Barnes — internal approvals and stakeholder alignment.
- Procurement: procurement@datasentry.com — contract execution.

Immediate asks (please):
1) Confirm procurement contact and legal reviewer.
2) Pick preferred QBR windows: Aug 31 (afternoon PT), Sep 1 (morning PT), Sep 2 (any). We'll lock a 60-minute slot.
3) Flag any non-standard contract clauses we should expect so Legal can pre-review (data retention, audit terms, indemnities).

Next steps from our side: Rishi will post two pricing scenarios (conservative + ramp) by EOD 8/16. I will send the DocuSign once we have confirmation on procurement contact and any redlines.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this buttoned up.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

- Procurement contact is Procurement Team <procurement@datasentry.com> (cc'd). Legal reviewer for the contract will be Samantha Lee (cc'd).
- We're aligned on the idea of a 12-month term; we do want to confirm the pricing math for the Pro tier before we lock.

1) Can you include a short runbook bullet on how you plan to throttle bursts and the expected failover behavior if capacity thresholds are hit? Our SRE team needs that for architecture approval.
2) We may have a standard procurement clause around data residency — I'll upload anything specific once legal reviews.

I'll wait for Rishi's pricing scenarios. If possible, please put a target turnaround on redlines — our legal SLA is typically 3 business days.

Subject: Re: Renewal kickoff: DataSentry commitment, capacity uplift & QBR scheduling

Alex, Samantha —

Attaching two quick scenarios (refer to capacity_pricing_2026-08.xlsx):
A) Conservative: +100k tokens/day uplift, maintain Standard tier (lower unit price, higher burst surtax). Estimated uplift spend: ~$12k/mo.
B) Pro-tier recommended: +200k tokens/day uplift, tier bump to Pro (predictable per-token rate, included burst allowances). Estimated uplift spend: ~$18k/mo but with lower effective = cost/token at scale.

Operational notes (runbook bullets) — short version for your SREs: 
- Throttling: continuous-batch queue with token-based rate limiting per API key; soft-queueing for spikes < 30s.
- Failover: automated fallback to a compatible smaller model variant (same API surface) if sustained latency > 2s for 60s window.
- Ramp plan: initial canary (10% traffic) for 72 hours after effective date, then 50% for 7 days, then full production.

If DataSentry needs retention or residency adjustments, that will affect on-prem/private deployment options; I'll sync with Solutions to scope any compliance changes.

I will finalize pricing in the sheet and mark a recommended scenario by EOD.

-Rishi
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
